changes.after: Mount ownership is explicit below. appendix:
## DY2 exact drawing fixtures and DY3 continuity

This appendix fixes the teaching entities for the ten previously underdetermined jobs. It is a design contract, not a new trajectory-run receipt. Exact algebra below is derived from the stated equations. The only bounded arithmetic used while preparing it is the four rational vector slope probes for D46; no retained programme or numerical campaign is executed. Mobile composition stacks the same linked objects in their stated reading order with exterior wrapping labels and unchanged coordinate meaning.

| Job | Exact default, construction and scale | Interpretation and narrow composition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D05 | Equilibrium 0, ε=1/2, δ=1/4; compare x′=−x and x′=x from x0=1/5 on t∈[0,2]. Plot x∈[−.6,.6], marking continuation of the unstable curve beyond the frame. The stable formula x0 exp(−t) obeys |x(t)|≤|x0|<δ<ε for every t≥0; the unstable curve crosses ε at ln(5/2). | Show the ±ε horizontal tube and ±δ initial segment on a time/state plane, then the two trajectories. The inequality establishes the stable case for all admissible starts; two plotted curves alone do not establish the quantified theorem. On a phone use two aligned plots with the same rulers, followed by the inequality. |
| D06 | All four start at x0=1/4. On t∈[0,4], use x0 exp(−t), x0/sqrt(1+2x0²t), x0 and x0/sqrt(1−2x0²t). Common vertical interval [0,.5]; the positive cubic pole is at t=8, outside the safe window. | Directly label exponential return, algebraic return, unchanged and departure; annotate the excluded pole in text, not by continuing its curve. Stack two paired plots if four labels collide, retaining identical scales and t=4 readouts. Source: direct separation of the four scalar ODEs and the preserved C02 formulas. |
| D07 | Use the explicitly constructed field F(q,p)=(−q+q²,−2p) at z*=(0,0). J=diag(−1,−2). For η=(.1,.1), Jη=(−.1,−.2), F(z*+η)−F(z*)=(−.09,−.2), remainder=(.01,0). Generally remainder=(ηq²,0), norm≤||η||². All vectors use equal coordinate scales on [−.25,.15]². | Place input disturbance beside a separate rate-vector plane; the latter joins the linear image to the actual difference by the remainder arrow. State that the Jacobian maps state disturbance to rate disturbance, not to a finite-time state. Stack the two planes and the short arithmetic row. No new model simulation is needed. |
| D08 | Flow examples: J=[[−1,−1],[1,−1]] has λ=−1±i; scalar λ=0 is boundary and λ=1 is outside. Map examples: M=[[.5,−.5],[.5,.5]] has μ=.5±.5i; scalar μ=1 is boundary and μ=1.2 outside. Both complex planes use real/imaginary axes [−1.5,1.5] with equal units; label λ as inverse time and μ as dimensionless. | Shade the strict left half-plane and strict unit disc separately; dashed boundary and direct eigenvalue labels. Boundary markers say linear test inconclusive for a nonlinear system, not stable. Stack flow then map and retain the two example matrices in adjacent text. The spectra follow the characteristic quadratics. |
| D12 | Pitchfork a=1: V=x⁴/4−x²/2 and W=V−V(1)=(x²−1)²/4. Take the positive-well component C={x>0:W≤1/64}=[sqrt(3)/2,sqrt(5)/2], wholly inside |x−1|<1/4. Plot x∈[.7,1.3], W∈[0,.08], the level 1/64, and arrows from both endpoints toward 1. Wdot=−(x−x³)²; its zero set within C is {1}. | Compactness is for this closed component, not the entire open half-line; the other well is excluded. Describe the largest invariant zero-derivative subset and why it is {1} here. Stack potential sublevel, phase line and set membership. The bounds and derivative are exact algebra. |
| D21 | Hopf a=1 at (q,p)=(3/10,2/5): r=1/2. Radial vector (a−r²)(q,p)=(9/40,3/10), tangential vector (−p,q)=(−2/5,3/10), sum=(−7/40,3/5). Thus r′=3/8, θ′=1. Use q,p axes [−.2,.7]×[−.1,1.1] with equal unit lengths, original point and a head-to-tail decomposition. | Both components are nonzero, so their distinct jobs are visible. State that this a=1 decomposition differs from the later a=.25 default cycle experiment. Stack the state ray/radius and velocity decomposition while retaining the same origin and component identities. |
| D31 | Logistic r=5/2, x0=1/5 gives x1=2/5,x2=3/5,x3=3/5. Derivative factors at x0,x1,x2 are 3/2,1/2,−1/2. Start tangent disturbance d0=1/1000: d1=3/2000,d2=3/4000,d3=−3/8000. Total factor −3/8; log magnitude sum ln(3/2)+ln(1/2)+ln(1/2)=ln(3/8). | Three local input/output planes use x∈[0,1]; tiny disturbance vectors get a clearly labelled magnified local scale, not a false full-axis width. The third factor reverses direction. Stack the three operations, then join their exact product/log row. Tangent displacements are linear approximations, not new exact perturbed-orbit measurements. |
| D35 | Use the constructed exponential error model e(n)=10⁻⁵ exp(.4n), n∈[0,25], tolerance ε=.02. The continuous crossing is n*=ln(2000)/.4; integer n=19 is below and n=20 above. Plot log10(error)∈[−5,−1], explicitly cropping later growth. Separately show one renormalization of tangent vector d=10⁻⁵ by gain exp(.4), record log gain .4, then rescale to 10⁻⁵. | This is a forecast-budget model under a constant local rate, not an empirical logistic exponent or a saturation claim. Noise, nonlinear departure and variable rates limit it. Stack budget curve then the marked rescale operation; distinguish accumulated log gain from the reset vector length. It deliberately reuses T09 parameters as an explained example, while T09 still requires a limitations diagnosis. |
| D46 | Lorenz F(q,p,z)=(10(p−q), q(28−z)−p, qp−(8/3)z), y0=(1,1,1), h=1/200. k1=F(y0), k2=F(y0+h k1/2), k3=F(y0+h k2/2), k4=F(y0+h k3); accepted y1=y0+h(k1+2k2+2k3+k4)/6. Exact rational trial states and slopes are in design-rk4-trial-r2.json. | Display four complete state/rate rows and their geometric q,p projections using q∈[.999,1.005],p∈[.99,1.14], with explicit unequal projection scales and all z values retained. A separate time strip marks 0,h/2,h/2,h; the middle pair are different trial states at the same time. Stack rows and strip on a phone. Do not draw these trial probes as four accepted trajectory steps. The full C12 execution remains a later content task. |
| D56 | Explicit constructed true map F(x)=x/2 and learned approximation G(x)=x/2+1/10, common x0=1, held-out evaluation indices n=0…4. True states: 1,1/2,1/4,1/8,1/16. Approximate rollout: 1,3/5,2/5,3/10,1/4. Errors: 0,1/10,3/20,7/40,3/16. Axes n∈[0,4], x∈[0,1.1]. Teacher-forced local defect G(xn)−F(xn)=.1; rollout error obeys en+1=.5en+.1. | The finite rollout is analytically constructed, with no fitted data, training run or performance claim. Feedback arrows return each model’s own state; a separate local-defect mark explains why a one-step score differs from rollout error. Stack the paired state traces and feedback operations while keeping the same scale and initial point. |

**Rotation bridge at the start of §10, before D49:** the earlier center in §4 uses q′=−p,p′=q, so from (1,0) it moves upward counterclockwise and solves (cos t,sin t). The numerical oscillator now uses q′=p,p′=−q, so the same initial point moves downward clockwise and solves (cos t,−sin t). This is an explicit convention change; replacing the earlier p by its negative connects the two coordinate descriptions. Both have radius and energy E=(q²+p²)/2 constant and period 2π. D49–53, their intermediate arrows and C10 must follow the clockwise equation; no old scientific source or output is changed.

**Order reconciliation:** D07 teaches a local Jacobian action on a disturbance before spectral tests. The actual planar center/nullcline refresher stays in §4 at D16–18: component-zero lines precede interpreting that planar field and its phase portrait, not the earlier general Jacobian definition. The research successor states this actual order.
